column1: # What enforces each requirement in this library's specs (0024-spec-format FR-011 - FR-014).
# mechanism: check | gate | review | none. by: "<repo>: <command>" for check and gate, the defining requirement for review, "-" for none.

column4: note
suite/layers.test.ts: every file of src imports only files of src by relative paths and @intellectual-frontiers/core by name, and no node: module
suite/layers.test.ts: the core imports neither dialects nor extensions and names no dialect but the base; a dialect imports the core and its parent dialects; an extension imports the core alone
suite/layers.test.ts: the manifest exports the core, every dialect folder and every extension folder, and no other library of commons imports a file of this one by a relative path
suite/lexer.test.ts: for any text and any dialect the lexer does not throw and ends, and every character is in one token, one comment or white space, in order, so the text can be put back

suite/lexer.test.ts: tokens are columns of a closed set of kinds that end with the end of the text, a keyword is found without regard to case, and a word with a character outside ASCII is never a keyword

suite/lexer.test.ts: what the dialect cannot read is an error value with its span and the lexer goes on: an unclosed comment, string or quoted identifier ends at the end of the text, and an unreadable character is a token of the error kind
suite/lexer.test.ts: strings and quoted identifiers are read as their dialect writes them: doubled quotes, backslashes, prefixes, long quotes and dollar quotes

suite/lexer.test.ts: numbers have fractions, exponents, an initial point, radix prefixes and underscores where the dialect says; parameters come in the styles of the dialect; an operator is the longest at its place
suite/comments.test.ts: every comment of every kind the dialect has is kept, with its kind, marker, span and text, and nesting follows the dialect

suite/comments.test.ts: a block comment that begins /*+ is a hint where the dialect has hints, one that begins /*! is a conditional comment where it has those, and elsewhere both are plain block comments
suite/comments.test.ts: a line comment whose marker needs a space after it is a comment only before white space, a control character or the end of the text
suite/comments.test.ts: a comment's place is given: how many tokens precede it, whether it is on a line of its own, whether a blank line follows, and whether it is closed
suite/comments.test.ts: what looks like a comment inside a string, a quoted identifier or another comment is not one

suite/comments.test.ts: a position is found from an offset: lines end at \n, \r\n or a lone \r, line and column count from 1 in UTF-16 units, and an offset outside the text is placed at its nearest end
suite/dialect.test.ts: a lexical compiles once into tables, and one that cannot be compiled is an error value that names the field and never a thrown error
suite/dialect.test.ts: a dialect is made from a name, its parent and a function from the parent's lexical, and can add, remove and replace what it inherits; a chain is resolved once
suite/dialect.test.ts: the base is ansi in the core, and SQLite, PostgreSQL and DuckDB each extend it with what their engines document
suite/speed.test.ts: the lexer has no regular expression, a token is no object, and it lexes the corpus at a floor of ten megabytes of text a second

suite/tree.test.ts: a tree is a closed union told apart by kind, a child field has the type of its sort so that a wrong sort or a missing case does not compile, and no node holds its parent or the text
suite/tree.test.ts: every node has a range, the ranges of children are inside their parent's, and a parenthesis at the edge of a node is inside it
suite/tree.test.ts: a name is an identifier with its quotes taken off or a qualified name, and a star keeps its qualifier
suite/tree.test.ts: a number keeps its text, a string its value as the dialect reads it and its prefix, and booleans, null and parameters are nodes of their own
suite/tree.test.ts: each kind of expression is a node of its own, with the fields the specification lists
suite/tree.test.ts: queries, sources, data changes and definitions have the nodes and fields the specification lists
suite/tree.test.ts: a script is a node of its statements and a statement the parser could not read is an unparsed node of its range
suite/parser.test.ts: parse accepts any text in any dialect, does not throw and ends, and parseStrict gives ok where there is no error and the errors where there is any
suite/parser.test.ts: expressions have the precedence of SQL and associate to the left
suite/parser.test.ts: set operations bind INTERSECT tighter and to the left, trailing clauses belong to the whole set operation, and a query may stand in parentheses wherever a query goes
suite/parser.test.ts: a word is an identifier where the dialect does not reserve it, a reserved word only after a dot or quoted, and an alias is read with or without AS

suite/parser.test.ts: what cannot be read is an error value with a span and a sentence, the next statement is read, the lexer's errors are among the errors, and deep nesting is an error and not a stack overflow
suite/parser.test.ts: a dialect's grammar adds its operators, cast and like-words, is checked against its lexical, and is inherited

suite/attach.test.ts: each comment is attached by one rule: leading to the child after it on a line of its own, detached where a blank line follows, trailing to the child before it where it shares the line, and dangling where nothing is near
suite/attach.test.ts: every comment of a text is in the table once, in order, for each node its own by placement, whether or not the statement around it was read
suite/walk.test.ts: children gives every child of every kind in the order of the text, walk visits depth first and can skip, findAll is typed by its kind, and fold combines from the leaves
suite/walk.test.ts: toSexp writes the same text for the same tree, and each golden file is what the parser makes of its SQL
suite/speed.test.ts: the parser reads tokens by index with no regular expression, and parses the corpus, comments attached, at a floor of three megabytes of text a second
suite/rewrite.test.ts: rules by sort are called from the leaves up for each node in a place of that sort, return a node of the same sort or nothing, and the result has the type of what was given

suite/rewrite.test.ts: a rewrite changes nothing it is given, returns the same object for what no rule changed and for the whole tree where nothing changed, and makes new objects only for a changed node and those above it
suite/rewrite.test.ts: a rewrite keeps the range of every node it does not replace, gives a replacement the range its rule gave it, and the builders take the range of what they stand for
suite/rewrite.test.ts: every kind of node is handled, a rule for identifiers is called for every identifier wherever it stands, and no tree the parser makes throws
suite/query.test.ts: the table of parents gives each node's parent once, the root has none, and ancestors come nearest first
suite/query.test.ts: a selection is lazy and can be read again, its methods are typed by the kind asked for, and its nodes come in the order of the text
suite/query.test.ts: each use of a table is given by name and access, in the order of the text, and a name of a common table expression in scope is not a table
suite/query.test.ts: every call is given with its name and node, and a script that is not one query says why it is not read-only
suite/unist.test.ts: each node has its kind as its type, children or a value, and a position of unist points
suite/unist.test.ts: data holds the fields that are not nodes, and a child says which field of its parent it is and its place in a list
suite/unist.test.ts: a comment is a node among the children of the node that encloses it, in the order of the text, with its data, and an unparsed statement keeps its comments and its source
suite/unist.test.ts: the projection changes nothing, is the same for the same input, and is a tree in the unist sense: objects with a string type, parents with arrays of children, no node twice

suite/unist.test.ts: unist-util-visit visits the projection by type and in order, unist-util-select selects with type, child, descendant and attribute selectors, and the nodes are assignable to the types of @types/unist
suite/docs.test.ts: the text of a comment has its markers taken off, whatever kind of comment the dialect has, and consecutive comments are joined by a new line
suite/docs.test.ts: a declaration is documented by its leading comments, its trailing comments and those that trail its name, and by no detached, dangling or other comment
suite/docs.test.ts: documentation has a summary, a description and tags, read as TSDoc reads them
suite/docs.test.ts: param, returns, example, deprecated, since and see are typed, every other tag is a tag with its name and text, and a project's reader is used in the place of the generic one
suite/docs.test.ts: the code of an example is the text of the tag without its fence, parsed with the dialect of the script, with its tree and errors

suite/docs.test.ts: a script gives, in order, its tables with columns and named constraints, views, indexes, common table expressions, added columns and other statements, each with its kind, name, node and documentation
suite/docs.test.ts: declarations are written as Markdown, one section for each that has documentation or members that have it, with the same text for the same declarations
suite/docs.test.ts: extracting documentation changes nothing it reads and gives the same result for the same input
suite/dialects.test.ts: the thirty dialects are modules of their own that are exports of the package, in the families of the specification, and what is not SQL is not among them
suite/dialects.test.ts: each dialect's lexical says its comments, identifiers, strings, prefixes, dollar quotes, parameters and numbers as its engine does
suite/dialects.test.ts: the lexer reads number suffixes, Oracle's alternative quoting and words that begin with a character a dialect names, and a lexical that gets them wrong is an error value
suite/dialects.test.ts: each dialect's grammar names its cast operator, like-words and operators as its engine documents them, and a dialect with nothing to add keeps its parent's
suite/dialects.test.ts: DAX, PRQL and Tableau are not dialects of this library, and the reason is written where the dialects are described

suite/conformance.test.ts: every corpus file has a row of provenance with its repository, commit, license and statements, the license is permissive and its text is kept, and what is included is in the register of third-party files

suite/conformance.test.ts: for every statement of every corpus in its dialect the lexer and the parser do not throw, every character is in a token, a comment or white space, ranges nest, comments are attached once, the projection and a rewrite with no rules hold, and a second run gives the same
suite/conformance.test.ts: the number of statements each file reads with no error does not fall below the baseline, the lexer's errors do not rise above it, and every file has a row
suite/conformance.test.ts: every dialect is read in a corpus of its own, or is listed as an exception in the provenance

suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: a statement that begins with a command word, and a CREATE, ALTER or DROP of an object the grammar does not read, is a command node with its keyword, object and text, and never an error
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: CREATE TABLE is read as a table made from a query, with no column list, and with the text after the columns or the name that the parser does not read kept as options
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: arrays are read as [a, b] and ARRAY[a, b], a subscript as x[i] that binds as tightly as ::, and [ is a quote where the dialect says so
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: VALUES is read as a source, with an alias and a column list
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: a dialect's grammar may name word operators with binding powers, which become operator nodes, and one whose word is not a keyword of its lexical is an error value
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: COLLATE is read after an expression as a node and after a data type as its collation

suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: a select is read with DISTINCT ON, GROUP BY ALL, the empty grouping and GROUPING SETS, a WINDOW clause and QUALIFY, and a frame with its EXCLUDE; QUALIFY stays a name where nothing but the end of an item follows it
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: a call is read with an ORDER BY among its arguments, WITHIN GROUP, and a query as an argument
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: TRY_CAST, SAFE_CAST and CAST ... FORMAT are casts, and a parenthesized join keeps its alias and may begin with a query
suite/routines.test.ts: a procedural statement ends at the first ; outside every block it opens, and every other statement at its first ;
suite/routines.test.ts: BEGIN begins a transaction where it is followed by ;, the end, or a word of a transaction, and a block elsewhere

suite/routines.test.ts: CREATE FUNCTION and CREATE PROCEDURE are a create-routine node with the object, replace, name, parameters, result, language and characteristics, and a header that is not read is a command
suite/routines.test.ts: a routine's body is a node with its style and text, and its offsets in the whole text where the text can be read in place
suite/routines.test.ts: PL/pgSQL is read as a block of declarations, statements and handlers, with every statement the specification lists
suite/routines.test.ts: the SQL a body holds is read with the core parser at its place in the whole text, and the INTO of a statement is taken out of it and kept
suite/routines.test.ts: the comments of a body are kept and attached to its nodes by the rule of the core

suite/routines.test.ts: what cannot be read is an error value with its span in the whole text, the statement is kept as unparsed or with a null in the place of the expression, and the statements after it are read
suite/routines.test.ts: every routine of the corpus of PL/pgSQL from PostgreSQL's tests is read without a throw, and the number whose body is read with no error does not fall below the baseline

suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: expressions are read with fields of rows, slices, typed literals, interval ranges, keyword arguments, null treatment, SIMILAR TO, NOT NULL, IS, IN with no list or a table, DEFAULT and star modifiers
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: a dialect with operator runs reads the operators it does not list, before and between operands, and a run does not end in a sign
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: data changes are read with conflict clauses, aliases, paths for columns, USING, and data changes in WITH
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: definitions are read with no columns, LIKE, column options, constraints with options, index and view options, and alter actions with options
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: queries are read with LIMIT offset and count, table hints, WITH ORDINALITY, semi and anti joins, joins that nest on the right, a USING alias, and a select with no items

suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: a dialect's grammar switches on a query that begins with FROM, lambdas, paths, indexes in CREATE TABLE, the tail of a query, parametric calls and TOP, and a dialect that does not switch them on reads as before
suite/grammar-growth.test.ts: struct literals, types with fields, ORDER BY ALL, BY NAME, upserts of MySQL and Hive, APPLY, table operators and hints, and the arguments of calls are read
suite/conformance.test.ts: no StarRocks corpus file holds the template variable `${...}` of its test runner, which is not SQL

suite/emit.test.ts: an identifier is quoted as the dialect's first syntax writes it, bare only where it is a plain lower-case word that is not a keyword, and a dialect with no quote gives an error value
suite/emit.test.ts: a string is written as the dialect's first string syntax writes it, and a quote that cannot be written inside is an error value
suite/emit.test.ts: what quoteIdent and quoteString give is read back as exactly one token of the same dialect's lexer, in every dialect
suite/emit.test.ts: the styles of a dialect are listed, a name takes the colon, at or dollar style, a position takes $n or ?, and a dialect without a fitting style gives an error value
suite/emit.test.ts: what placeholder gives is read back as exactly one parameter token of the same dialect's lexer, in every dialect that has a style that fits
suite/registry.test.ts: a registry holds ansi, adds a dialect found by name without regard to case, refuses a name taken or a parent that is not registered, and takes the same dialect twice

suite/registry.test.ts: functions are registered per dialect, found without regard to case in the dialect and then in those it extends, and a function that cannot be is an error value that changes nothing
suite/registry.test.ts: no function of the registry or of quoting throws for an unusual value
